### Theorem
For every type-\(A\) bigrassmannian \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\), both families
\[
G_L=\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\},\qquad
G_R=\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}
\]
minimally generate \(J_v\subseteq A=\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\). Moreover
\[
Q:=J_v/A_+J_v\cong\bigoplus_{\rho\subseteq b^a}\mathbb Z\,e_\rho,
\qquad \deg e_\rho=ij+|\rho|,
\]
and each family maps to a homogeneous integral basis of \(Q\). Hence
\[
H_Q(z)=z^{ij}\binom{a+b}{a}_z,
\]
and \(Q_d\) is torsion-free, vanishing unless \(ij\le d\le ij+ab\).

### Hypotheses
\[
1\le t\le r,s\le n,\qquad t>r+s-n,
\]
\[
i=s-t+1,\quad j=r-t+1,\quad
a=\min(n-r-i,r-j),\quad b=\min(i,j).
\]
Here \(A_+\) is the positive-degree ideal of \(A\), and bars denote images in \(A\).

For \(a=2\),
\[
\rank Q_{ij+N}=
\begin{cases}
\lfloor N/2\rfloor+1,&0\le N\le b,\\
\lfloor(2b-N)/2\rfloor+1,&b\le N\le2b,\\
0,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
For \(a=3\), \(\rank Q_{ij+N}=R_b(N)\), with \(R_b(N)=R_b(3b-N)\), and
\[
R_b(N)=
\begin{cases}
0,&N<0\text{ or }N>3b,\\
P(N),&0\le N\le b,\\
P(N)-P(N-b-1)-P(N-b-2)-P(N-b-3),
&b<N\le\lfloor3b/2\rfloor,
\end{cases}
\]
where \(P(t)=0\) for \(t<0\), and, for \(t=6u+r\), \(0\le r<6\),
\[
(P(6u+r))_{r=0}^5=
(3u^2+3u+1,\,3u^2+4u+1,\,3u^2+5u+2,\,
3u^2+6u+3,\,3u^2+7u+4,\,3u^2+8u+5).
\]

### Consolidated proof
By `-296-1`, the lower-family residue map
\[
\bigoplus_{\rho\subseteq b^a}\mathbb Z e_\rho\longrightarrow Q,\qquad
e_\rho\mapsto[\bar s_{(i^j,\rho)}],
\]
is a graded integral isomorphism. Thus the lower residues are a homogeneous basis of \(Q\).

By `-301-1` and `-264-1`, partition conjugation gives an integral graded isomorphism on the corresponding indecomposable quotients. The admissibility and endpoint identification certified in `-286-1` carry the conjugate lower basis to the right-family residue basis. Hence the right residues are also a homogeneous integral basis.

Each family is already a generating family for \(J_v\) in the certified constructions. If one generator could be removed while retaining generation of \(J_v\), its image could be removed while retaining generation of \(Q\). This contradicts that the images are bases. Thus both families are minimal.

The lower basis has one element \(e_\rho\) in degree \(ij+|\rho|\) for each \(\rho\subseteq b^a\). Therefore
\[
H_Q(z)=z^{ij}\sum_{\rho\subseteq b^a}z^{|\rho|}
=z^{ij}\binom{a+b}{a}_z.
\]
The complement involution
\[
\rho\longmapsto(b-\rho_a,\ldots,b-\rho_1)
\]
gives a perfect integral pairing
\[
Q_d\times Q_{2ij+ab-d}\to\mathbb Z.
\]
The stated \(a=2\) and \(a=3\) rank formulas follow from the certified partition counts in `-320-1` and `-326-1`.

### Optional statements
- No universal marked transition matrix between the ordered \(G_L\)- and \(G_R\)-bases is asserted.
- No claim is made for arbitrary Schubert ideals \(I_w\) beyond the bigrassmannian basic ideals \(J_v\).
- A closed quasi-polynomial formula for arbitrary \(a\) is not used here.

### Verdict
Established. The requested theorem-boundary consolidation proves the original two-family minimality target, together with the integral graded structure of \(J_v/A_+J_v\).
